Technology

The Stack We Support in Production

We list what we genuinely build, deploy and maintain for clients. A shorter list, supported properly, is worth more to you than a longer one nobody on the team has run at scale.

Get a Free ConsultationExplore Our Services
FrontendBackendDatabasesCloudDevOpsIntegrationAI & Automation

Frontend

Interfaces built with standards first and framework code only where it earns its place.

  • ReactComponent-driven UIs and single-page applications
  • AngularStructured enterprise front ends with TypeScript
  • JavaScriptModern ES modules, no unnecessary tooling
  • TypeScriptType safety on larger front-end codebases
  • HTMLSemantic markup as the accessibility and SEO baseline
  • CSSResponsive layout with Grid, Flexbox and custom properties

Backend

Application and API layers chosen for the workload rather than for novelty.

  • .NETASP.NET Core web applications and Web APIs
  • C#Primary language for enterprise and Azure-hosted services
  • PythonAutomation, data processing and AI integration work
  • Node.jsEvent-driven services, APIs and build tooling
  • REST APIsVersioned, documented service contracts

Databases

Relational by default, document stores where the access pattern justifies them.

  • SQL ServerTransactional workloads and reporting
  • PostgreSQLOpen-source relational workloads at scale
  • MySQLWeb application and commerce back ends
  • MongoDBDocument storage for flexible schemas
  • RedisCaching, sessions and rate limiting

Cloud

Two platforms, supported properly, rather than a logo wall of every provider.

  • Microsoft AzureApp Service, Azure SQL, Functions, AKS, Storage, Key Vault
  • AWSEC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, API Gateway, CloudFront, IAM

DevOps

Reproducible environments and releases that do not depend on one person's laptop.

  • DockerConsistent packaging across environments
  • KubernetesOrchestration where the workload justifies it
  • CI/CDAutomated build, test and release pipelines
  • GitHubSource control, reviews and GitHub Actions
  • Azure DevOpsRepos, boards and release pipelines
  • TerraformInfrastructure defined as reviewable code

Integration

The connective layer between applications, platforms and third-party services.

  • REST & Web APIsPrimary integration style across our work
  • WebhooksEvent-driven integration with signature verification
  • OAuth 2.0 / JWTDelegated authorisation and token-based auth
  • Azure Service BusReliable messaging between decoupled systems

Model access through server-side APIs, with logging and cost controls in place.

  • Claude APIDocument processing, drafting and assisted search

  • Vector searchRetrieval over your own documents and records
  • Workflow automationRule-based automation of approvals and data flows

How we choose

Why This List and Not a Longer One

The best technology for your project is usually the one that is well understood, well supported and easy to hire for — not the one that was released last quarter.

We choose a stack against four questions: does it fit the workload, can it be operated by whoever runs it after us, is there a real support and security track record, and does it lock you into a single vendor unnecessarily.

Where something newer genuinely solves a problem the established option cannot, we will make that case explicitly and explain the trade-off. What we will not do is introduce an unfamiliar framework to a client project as a learning exercise.

Working with what you already have

If your systems run on something not listed here, that is not automatically a problem. We regularly integrate with platforms we would not choose to build on.

  • Legacy databases and internal applications
  • Third-party SaaS with a documented API
  • ERP and CRM platforms of most vendors
  • Existing codebases from a previous team

We will review it honestly and tell you if maintaining it is a poor use of your budget.

Architecture

Bring the requirements and constraints. We will recommend an architecture and explain why — including the trade-offs.
